reviews.comment: Dr. Schneider was not an engaging lecturer. Phys 206 is designed to have students read the textbook ahead of in class lectures, but if you did so you would gain very little from his lectures as they're mostly just a rehashing of the textbook. I don't think he wrote the exams, but they were brutal for someone who knew the content in advance.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures involved a lot of practice problems and could be hard to follow at times. Exams were difficult but they were common exams so that was true with every section of the class. He seems to care about the content and is a nice guy. If you can pay attention during lecture he is an overall good professor.

His lectures consisted of reading off of slides and doing basic practice problems. When we would bring example problems he would solve them in the most complicated way possible. I just do not think he taught the class very well at all. I had to do a lot of outside learning and practice. Overall, the class is hard and I do not think he helps.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures were boring, and sometimes he solved problems in the most complicated way. He did a good job of answering questions, and he seems like a nice guy. This class, however, is no joke after the first exam. Reading the textbook is honestly mandatory, as you will fall behind and not understand lectures if you don't keep up with the readings.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He intentionally made exams 2 and 3 harder than usual because the previous exam average was higher than expected, which, of course, resulted in the average exam grade failing for midterms 2 and 3. Lectures do not include enough practice problems, and he briefly touches on concepts that are very pivotal on tests.

At the beginning of the semester he was very interactive during his lectures because he would work out the problems on the board. However, after the first midterm he started working problems on the computer where he clicks through the equations and tries to explain them. He is a very nice professor and is one of the better options for PHYS206.

He was good at the beginning of the semester but then he stopped working out problems on the board and made everything digital so now he explains his work instead of working through it. It can be hard to pay attention when he's just explaining his work instead of working through it. But based on the options of physics professors, he's good.
